findings.title: Blocked email lookup is case-sensitive and trivially bypassed
findings.body: `should_block?` looks up the record with `BlockedEmail.where(email: email)`, an exact, case-sensitive comparison. Neither the stored value nor the incoming value is normalized with `Email.downcase`/strip, and the unique index is also case-sensitive. If `bad@spammers.org` is blocked, a user can register as `Bad@Spammers.org` and the block does not fire. Normalize emails on save and before the lookup.

findings.title: Non-atomic match_count increment loses updates under concurrent signups
findings.body: The counter is updated by read-modify-write: load the record, do `match_count += 1` in Ruby, then `save`. Concurrent validations for the same email read the same value and overwrite each other, so increments are lost. Use an atomic SQL update instead, e.g. `update_all(['match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ?', now])` or `increment_counter`.

findings.title: Validator writes to the DB on every validation, inflating match statistics
findings.body: `BlockedEmail.should_block?` updates match_count and last_match_at every time validation runs. `UsersController#create` validates twice: once via `user.valid?` (outside any transaction, before the DiscourseHub call) and again via `user.save`. For `:do_nothing` entries both writes commit, so each signup is counted twice. Any other `valid?` call also inflates the counts. A validator should not have persistent side effects; record the match once at the point of an actual signup attempt.

findings.title: rejectedEmails array is defined on the prototype and shared/persistent
findings.body: `rejectedEmails: Em.A([])` is defined in `extend`, so a single array lives on the class prototype. Every instance shares it, and it is never reset when the modal is reopened. An email rejected once, for any email error including transient ones, stays marked invalid on the client for the rest of the page session, even if the admin later unblocks it. Initialize the array in `init` and clear it when the modal is shown.

findings.title: New error/values fields in create response are untested
findings.body: The client now depends on `errors` and `values.email` being present in the failure response from `create`. No controller spec covers these fields or the blocked-email signup path end to end, so a regression would silently break the client-side rejected-email handling.
